content: Apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1 (ASK1), also referred to as mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 5 (MAP3K5), is a member of the MAP kinase kinase kinase family. It plays a critical role in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway. ASK1 is responsible for activating c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) and p38 MAP kinases in a manner that does not depend on Raf signaling. This activation occurs in response to various cellular stressors, including oxidative stress, endoplasmic reticulum stress, and calcium influx. ASK1 has been implicated in the pathogenesis of several diseases, including cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and neurodegenerative disorders. The protein encoded by the MAP3K5 gene consists of 1,374 amino acids and contains 11 kinase subdomains. Northern blot analysis has revealed that MAP3K5 transcripts are highly expressed in human heart and pancreas tissues. Under non-stress conditions, ASK1 exists in an oligomerized state, which is necessary for its activation. This oligomerization is mediated by its C-terminal coiled-coil domain (CCC). However, ASK1 remains inactive due to the suppressive effects of reduced thioredoxin (Trx) and calciumand integrin-binding protein 1 (CIB1). Trx directly binds to the N-terminal coiled-coil domain (NCC) of ASK1, thereby inhibiting its kinase activity. Trx and CIB1 regulate ASK1 activation in a redox-sensitive and calcium-sensitive manner, respectively. Both Trx and CIB1 appear to compete with tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) receptor-associated factor 2 (TRAF2), which is an activator of ASK1. Upon activation, TRAF2 and TRAF6 are recruited to ASK1, forming a larger molecular complex. ASK1 subsequently undergoes homo-oligomeric interactions through both its CCC and NCC domains. This process leads to the full activation of ASK1 via autophosphorylation at threonine 845. ASK1 has been shown to interact with a variety of proteins, including: C-Raf, CDC25A, DAXX, DUSP19, EIF2AK2, GADD45B, HSPA1A, MAP2K6, MAP3K7, MAPK8IP3, PDCD6, PPP5C, RB1CC1, TRAF2, TRAF5, and TRAF6.
